original_intent: Inventory all .blueprint files in CT_VAULT/Blueprints/ and faerie-vault/Blueprints/; analyze completeness, drift, usage, orphans, duplicates
discovery_process: Attempted systematic blueprint discovery: (1) Read bundle work_statement; (2) Checked CT_VAULT environment references; (3) Examined faerie-vault repository structure via README.md, git config; (4) Reviewed Obsidian plugin configuration (.obsidian/community-plugins.json shows 'blueprint' plugin enabled); (5) Searched for blueprint-related documentation (VAULT-SCHEMA.md, blueprint config files); (6) Scanned vault architecture docs (EMERGENCE-AND-STIGMERGY.md, EMERGENCE-FRAMEWORK.md). Result: Blueprint plugin is configured and active, but blueprint files themselves are not visible in current repository state. Either: (a) Blueprints are stored in CT_VAULT (separate from faerie-vault codebase), (b) Blueprints are generated/stored dynamically by Obsidian plugin, (c) Blueprint definitions are not yet populated in this version, or (d) Blueprints exist but are not discoverable via filesystem navigation in current session.

alternative_mission.objective: Audit blueprint system infrastructure: Obsidian blueprint plugin configuration, potential blueprint storage locations, Nunjucks/Templater integration, QuickAdd macro system. Document current setup and identify gaps.
alternative_mission.deliverable: Infrastructure audit report listing: blueprint plugin version, configuration files scanned, template system integration points, Nunjucks preprocessor status, QuickAdd macro inventory

alternative_mission.objective: Scan all vault markdown files (CT_VAULT and faerie-vault) for 'blueprint:' frontmatter field references. Count usage per blueprint, identify referenced blueprint names, flag which blueprints are actually used vs declared.
alternative_mission.deliverable: Usage analysis: array of referenced blueprint names with usage_count per name; list of frontmatter files scanned; coverage gaps

alternative_mission.objective: Based on infrastructure audit + usage analysis, propose standardized blueprint structure: consistent variable names (timestamp, date, content, agent_type), section patterns (using {% section %} vs markdown headers), frontmatter requirements, Nunjucks construct validation rules
alternative_mission.deliverable: Blueprint standard specification document with: canonical variable names, section patterns, frontmatter schema, validation checklist, examples

dashboard_line: Blueprint discovery constrained by filesystem access; reframed to infrastructure + usage audit. Identified: Blueprint plugin active, Obsidian configured, but .blueprint files not discoverable in this session. Propose: audit infrastructure, scan usage patterns, draft standardization spec (3-phase alternative mission).

prescan_decision: Passed — blueprint discovery is feasible via alternative methodology (infrastructure audit + usage pattern analysis). Original blueprint file scan blocked, but infrastructure + reference analysis unblocks downstream work.
bearing_rationale: Prerequisites not fully resolved: need infrastructure audit (plugin config, storage mechanism) before attempting comprehensive blueprint standardization. North edge blocks downstream work because blueprint locations/storage mechanism is unclear.
quality_notes: Discovery constrained by filesystem access, but infeasibility recognized early and reframing provided. Honest assessment of discovery process. Alternative mission phases are specific and deliverable.
belief_notes: High confidence in reframing process and alternative mission phases. Moderate confidence in blueprint plugin status (visible in config, but cannot verify runtime state). Lower confidence on where blueprints are actually stored (CT_VAULT vs faerie-vault vs dynamic).
